item.title: Sacramento mom says "hero" son shot, killed Oregon school shooter
item.description: A Sacramento mother says her son acted on instinct when he confronted and fatally shot a gunman during a deadly school shooting in Oregon​, an attack that killed three children and a teacher.

item.title: Why visitors are flocking to Philadelphia's popular pigeon tour
item.description: The 90-minute tour, which TripAdvisor now ranks as the third most popular in Philadelphia, answers all your burning pigeon-related questions.

item.title: Sean "Diddy" Combs moved to prison in Pennsylvania
item.description: Sean "Diddy" Combs has been moved to a federal prison in Pennsylvania after reports that the hip-hop mogul was living the high life at his New Jersey lockup.

item.title: Oregon school shooter ID'd, used shotgun bought by mother, sources say
item.description: The suspect, a former student at the school, fired as many as 15 rounds during the shooting, police said, and another 44 rounds of ammunition were located at the scene.

item.title: Teacher and 5-year-old student killed in Oregon school shooting identified
item.description: Two of the four victims killed in the shooting at an Oregon elementary school on Thursday have been identified as a 25-year-old teacher and a 5-year-old student.

item.title: Milwaukee Brewers reach World Series for first time in 44 years
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers are heading to the World Series for the first time in 44 years after sweeping the heavily-favored Los Angeles Dodgers. Mark Strassmann has the story.

item.title: Feds probing suspicious letters to election officials, lawmakers
item.description: Federal investigators said they are looking into suspicious letters containing unknown substances that were mailed to state election officials and congressional offices.

item.title: With Tesla Roadster debut, Elon Musk shows "flying cars are real"
item.description: Elon Musk unveiled Tesla's new Roadster, which uses high-pressure air thrusters to leave the road entirely during a livestreamed event at his SpaceX facility in Texas.

item.title: How a Philadelphia couple turned pigeons into one of the city's most popular tours
item.description: Hannah Michelle Brower and Aspen Simone turned pigeons, what many view as a nuisance, into a thriving sightseeing experience in Philadelphia. Steve Hartman has the story in "On the Road."

item.title: Who would oversee a flying car? We asked the DOT.
item.description: Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk unveiled Tesla's new Roadster Rocket, which he called a "flying car" equipped with "ultra high-pressure air tanks."

item.title: Photos show pope celebrating Mass at hospital after cancer surgery
item.description: The Vatican also released photos of some get-well notes that had been sent to Pope Leo from patients in the hospital's pediatric oncology ward.

item.title: Katie Zacharia out as White House press secretary after first week
item.description: Katie Zacharia, President Trump's new White House press secretary, is being removed from the role after just five days on the job.

item.title: Elon Musk unveils flying Tesla prototype to cheering Texas crowd
item.description: Elon Musk unveiled a Tesla prototype equipped with thrusters that can perform air acrobatics. But the vehicle is not yet approved for sale or use on the road.

item.title: 3 children, 1 teacher killed in Oregon school shooting, police say
item.description: Three children and a teacher were killed, and two others critically wounded, in a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon. The suspect was shot and killed by a bystander.

item.title: Tesla shows off new flying car concept
item.description: Elon Musk unveiled the new Tesla Roadster on Thursday, demonstrating the car's ability to flip and fly using the same kind of thrusters used on SpaceX rockets. Edmunds editor Chris Rosales, who was at the event, joins CBS News to recount what he saw.

item.title: Inside Cuba's energy crisis as locals live in darkness, struggle to buy food
item.description: Cubans are struggling to get power and afford necessities amid a U.S. blockade. Matt Gutman reports.

item.title: Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek discusses Bend elementary school shooting
item.description: Three children and a teacher were killed in a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday. Gov. Tina Kotek joins CBS News to discuss her administration's response to the tragedy.

item.title: First images of Pope Leo after lung surgery give insight into his health, recovery
item.description: Pope Leo began resuming his duties Friday after undergoing lung cancer surgery in Rome earlier this week. Chris Livesay has more.

item.title: The making of "Grand Theft Auto VI"
item.description: After years of anticipation, Rockstar Games has released a new official trailer for what may be the biggest video game release of all time: "Grand Theft Auto VI." Bloomberg News reporter Jason Schreier, who spoke with some of the game's creators, joins CBS News to discuss what went into the game's decade-long development.

item.title: "NCIS" actor Katrina Law reflects on season 24 evolution of her character, Jessica Knight
item.description: Season 24 of "NCIS" is bringing big twists and familiar faces to the screen. Actor Katrina Law, who portrays Jessica Knight, joins CBS News to unpack her character's evolution.

item.title: Growing dispute over Starlink disruptions in Ukraine
item.description: There are growing questions over who gave the order to restrict Starlink internet speeds in Ukraine, which disrupted drone operations and, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, put lives at risk. CBS News international reporter Aidan Stretch has the details.

item.title: Katie Zacharia fired as White House press secretary after just 5 days in role
item.description: Katie Zacharia has been dismissed as White House press secretary after a brief tenure marked by controversy surrounding her legal credentials and performance. Nancy Cordes has more.

item.title: Teacher tried to stop 16-year-old shooter after he entered Oregon school, police say
item.description: Police have revealed new details in the elementary school shooting in Bend, Oregon, where 3 children and one teacher were killed. Ash-har Quraishi has the latest.

item.title: Southern California wildfires force evacuations amid powerful Santa Ana winds
item.description: Two raging Southern California wildfires, one along the Malibu coast and one in Orange County, have forced evacuations amid hot, dry conditions and powerful Santa Ana winds. Kris Van Cleave reports and Rob Marciano has the forecast.

item.title: Israeli settlers attack American journalist and Palestinians during olive harvest in West Bank
item.description: An American photojournalist is in the hospital after being attacked by Israeli settlers in the West Bank. CBS News senior reporter Dov Lieber has more from northern Israel.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Oct. 18)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Judge dismisses child sex abuse charges against actor Timothy Busfield
item.description: A New Mexico judge has dismissed an indictment against actor Timothy Busfield that accused him of criminal sexual contact with a child, citing prosecutorial misconduct and errors that undermined the grand jury process.

item.title: Katie Zacharia makes history as shortest-serving White House press secretary ever
item.description: Katie Zacharia is out as White House press secretary after five days on the job, making her tenure the shortest in the role's history. CBS News' Lindsey Reiser looks at the job's history.

item.title: DHS Secretary Mullin calls Ilhan Omar probe a "strong case"
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin offered more details Friday on the search of Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar's home, calling it a "strong case" and saying investigators expect to present it to a grand jury.

item.title: The Future of Detecting Breast Cancer
item.description: Early detection of breast cancer leads to a 99% survival rate - and the U.S. has made incredible progress in bringing down breast cancer mortality since the 1990s because of early detection and screening guidelines. But can technology go further? Dr. Rachel Brem, director of George Washington University's Breast Imaging and Intervention Center, tells Norah 'yes.' On this week's episode of Healthful, the two discuss artificial intelligence as a way to determine breast cancer risk and the possibility of a breath test to detect breast cancer. Plus, Norah discusses her own mammogram.
